entities.summary: Egon Bretscher was a Swiss-born British chemist and nuclear physicist and Head of the Nuclear Physics Division from 1948 to 1966 at the Atomic Energy Research Establishment, also known as Harwell Laboratory, in Harwell, United Kingdom. He was one of the pioneers in nuclear fission research and one of the first to foresee that plutonium could be used as an energy source. His work on nuclear physics led to his involvement in the British atomic bomb research project Tube Alloys and his membership of the British Mission to the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos, where he worked in Enrico Fermi's Advanced Development Division in the F-3 Super Experimentation group.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bretscher's work on nuclear fission research and his foresight on plutonium as an energy source contributed to the development of the British atomic bomb project Tube Alloys. His involvement in the Manhattan Project led to significant advancements in nuclear physics.
